prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots rank B027 first, but I do not treat that as the argument. The merit is that the chain from mechanism to patient benefit is unusually complete: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect (Holst, Drucker), identification of the active GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov), and receptor-agonist therapies that lower glucose and weight and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit in large independent randomized trials. It opened a new physiological understanding of gut-pancreas-brain signalling, not only a drug. Maturity is not in doubt, and the clinical and societal effect is already among the largest of any recent discovery. A prize for the physiology, credited to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, fits the committee's tradition of rewarding discovery, with the drug development acknowledged in the citation.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real. Priority for the active-peptide work is disputed, Habener and others are outside the credited names, and Knudsen's development of long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide) is arguably what produced the clinical impact, so a three-person cap forces either a physiology-only prize that underweights the drug or a mixed one that excludes someone with a strong claim. If the committee cannot defend the attribution, B025 is the strongest fallback because it is a clean concept-to-cure chain, though it has its own Eshhar problem.

responses.point: Svenningsson would credit Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B027, replacing Mojsov with Knudsen as the person who led the pharmacological engineering of long-acting analogues, and he sees Mojsov's weighting as disputed.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen point seriously, since without long-acting analogues there is no therapy at this scale. But the Nobel tradition for this prize is to reward the discovery, and Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-37) form is the molecular step on which both the physiology and the later drug design depend. Knudsen's work was the optimisation of a known peptide in an industrial setting. I would keep Mojsov and say in the citation that the discovery enabled the therapies. I accept that this is a judgement call, and I would not oppose Knudsen if the committee finds the priority claims for Mojsov cannot be substantiated.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked cGAS-STING (B020) second, as a clear and original mechanism that unified antiviral defence, autoimmunity and cancer immunity, with a clean Chen and Barber configuration, and recognised that therapeutic translation is still immature.
responses.response: I agree that the mechanism is original and that the Chen and Barber attribution is the cleanest on the list. From the autoimmunity side I can also say that STING-associated vasculopathy and interferonopathies show human disease relevance. But I would hold that maturity point more strongly than he does: STING agonists and antagonists have not yet delivered a clinical result. The case rests on conceptual impact, and I find that a weaker basis for a prize this year than B027, where both concept and outcome exist. I keep B020 as a serious alternative, not the lead.

responses.point: El Manira ranked optogenetics (B035) second as a general method for causal, millisecond-precision control of defined cell types, with Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann as the proposed trio, and acknowledged that Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck have strong claims.
responses.response: The methodological influence is very large and I do not doubt it. My reservation is the one he raises himself: a three-person cap leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, who each have a documented claim, so any configuration contains an exclusion that is hard to justify. It is also a tool, and its therapeutic use (vision restoration) is only now starting. I would rate it below B027 and B025 on attribution, though I would not dismiss it if colleagues think the committee can defend the Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth selection.

responses.point: Sandberg ranked the unfolded protein response (B043) third, as a conceptually clean, conserved organelle-to-nucleus signalling mechanism with a natural two-person Walter and Mori attribution, and judged recognition arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution is cleaner than for most candidates, and that the UPR is a textbook mechanism relevant to secretory disease and neurodegeneration. My hesitation is that the link to human disease and to patient benefit is indirect, and I would want evidence that it is a discovery in medicine and not only in cell biology. I would put it below B027 and B025, but I would be willing to pair it with another part if the committee wants a two-achievement configuration.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide can be substantiated against Habener's group, which is not among the credited names.
Whether the committee should credit physiology alone or include the pharmaceutical development (Knudsen) within the three-person limit.
Whether B025 would be better served by a different set of names than the supplied credit, given Eshhar's earlier chimeric-receptor work.
The proposal I ranked second at opening (anti-TNF therapy in rheumatoid arthritis) is not on the shortlist, so I have not discussed it further here.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B027 or the other shortlisted candidates. My field is autoimmunity and rheumatology, so I am most familiar with B020 and B025 immunology, but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited name. Co-authors Kuchroo and Sonesson are not on the shortlist, and a shared Karolinska setting does not by itself establish a connection.
